clue.text: Roman consul and commander, champion lacking aspiration

parts.note: CIC is the abbreviation for commander-in-chief

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the letter for aspiration is dropped

parts.note: a champion is a hero
aspiration is the breathy sound written as H

explanation.surface: A description of a Roman leader who was a great soldier but did not aspire to much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aspiration' is the phonetic term for the H sound, so a champion 'lacking aspiration' is HERO said with a dropped H.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Tullius Cicero, the great orator, held the office of consul in Rome in 63 BC.

clue.text: Very unpleasant cold food for breakfast, not good

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

indicators.note: not removes the letter for good

parts.note: gruel is a thin porridge eaten for breakfast

explanation.surface: A complaint about a nasty, cold breakfast that is no good.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruel means causing pain or distress deliberately, which is very unpleasant.

clue.text: Business trick I rejected as dubious practice

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business

indicators.note: rejected means turned away, so the I is left out

parts.note: an illusion is a magic trick

explanation.surface: A company's scam is ruled a shady practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Collusion is secret cooperation to deceive or cheat, an underhand arrangement.

clue.text: Official law is something completely thoughtless

parts.note: a ref is a referee, a match official
lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: A referee's ruling being dismissed as utterly unthinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflex is an involuntary response that happens without conscious thought.

clue.text: Appeal breaking heart, flipping exciting

indicators.note: flipping turns the whole combination over so it is read backwards
the appeal word breaks into the heart word, splitting it apart

parts.note: the heart of something is its core
IT is slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Something sexy is so appealing it breaks your heart, and 'flipping' is a mild British intensifier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appeal' here is IT, the old slang for sex appeal, not a plea; and 'flipping' is not an intensifier but the reversal of the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erotic arouses sexual desire, so it is exciting in that sense.

clue.text: Drink up, embracing one working in local

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so the drink word wraps the others
in a down clue up means the word reads from the bottom, so it is backwards

parts.note: lager is a drink
I is the Roman numeral one
on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: Drink up, says someone hugging a worker in the pub; a local is a British neighbourhood pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' looks like the pub, but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Regional means relating to a particular area, so nearby or local in scope.

clue.text: However briefly, one may paint Nordic woman

parts.note: tho' is a shortened though, which means however
an RA, a Royal Academician, is a painter

explanation.surface: An artist sketching a Scandinavian woman, however briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: Thora is a female given name of Scandinavian origin, from the god Thor.

clue.text: Spooned jam scoffed by roguish individual

indicators.note: scoffed by means eaten up by, so the jam word sits inside the rogue word

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man
to jam or noodle is to improvise loosely on an instrument

explanation.surface: A rogue gobbles jam straight off a spoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooned' and 'jam' suggest food, but spooning is old slang for kissing and cuddling, and jam is the musical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To canoodle is to kiss and cuddle amorously, which is what spooning lovers do.

clue.text: Bit of heart from luvvie CBS paid to broadcast

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A US TV network pays a theatrical luvvie for a heartfelt broadcast; a luvvie is British slang for a gushing actor.
explanation.definitionFit: The bicuspid or mitral valve is the two-flapped valve in the heart between left atrium and ventricle.

clue.text: Heat magazine's contents, after modifying

indicators.note: after places the ammunition word behind the grammar word

parts.note: in grammar a word that modifies another is qualifying it
the magazine of a gun holds rounds of ammunition

explanation.surface: Heat is a British celebrity magazine, so this reads like an editor altering its contents.
explanation.walkthrough: Heat looks like the magazine's title, but it is the definition; the magazine is a gun's, holding a round.
explanation.definitionFit: A heat is a preliminary race or contest whose winners go on to the next stage of a competition.

clue.text: Bungling copper caught scoundrel with gold

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a louse is a contemptible person
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A clumsy policeman nabs a crook who is carrying gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Clouseau is the inept French detective played by Peter Sellers in the Pink Panther films.

clue.text: One addressing envelopes in other apparent order

indicators.note: the envelopes of these words are their outside letters, first and last of each

explanation.surface: Someone writing addresses on envelopes finds them in a different order than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One addressing envelopes' reads like a clerk writing addresses; the definition stops at 'addressing', and 'envelopes' is the device.
explanation.definitionFit: An orator is a public speaker, someone who addresses an audience.

clue.text: Auditor's rule check

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the word is as heard rather than as written

parts.note: to reign is to rule as monarch

explanation.surface: An accountant's regulation about checking the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests an accountant, but here it means a hearer.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein something in is to check or restrain it, as a rider does a horse.

clue.text: Ground-breaking device unaffected by revolution?

indicators.note: turning the word round leaves it the same, so it reads identically backwards

parts.note: a machine that breaks up the soil

explanation.surface: A pioneering invention that weathered a political revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground-breaking' sounds like innovative, but the device literally breaks up soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rotavator is a motorised cultivator with rotating blades that tills soil.

clue.text: Lead everyone around place to cooperate

indicators.note: the lead and everyone letters go around the word for place

parts.note: PB is the chemical symbol for lead
to lay something is to place it
everyone is all

explanation.surface: An instruction to guide a group around a venue so that they work together.
explanation.definitionFit: To play ball is an idiom for going along with others' wishes and being helpful.

clue.text: Hypnotic voice, overwhelming bass

indicators.note: overwhelming means engulfing, so the voice word swallows the bass letter

parts.note: a baritone is a male singing voice
B is the abbreviation for bass in music

explanation.surface: A mesmerising singer whose voice drowns out the bass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hypnotic' reads as an adjective, but it is the noun for a sleep-inducing drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbitone is a barbiturate sedative, a drug that induces sleep.

clue.text: Dance of Bedouin, say, in desert

indicators.note: in places the Bedouin word within the desert word

parts.note: a desert is a place of sand
a Bedouin is an example of an Arab

explanation.surface: A traditional dance performed by Bedouin in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: A saraband is a slow stately Spanish dance in triple time.

clue.text: One who hums reggae saving money, by the way

indicators.note: saving here means keeping inside, so the music word holds the money

parts.note: ska is the Jamaican music that led to reggae
tin is old slang for money
RD is short for road, a way

explanation.surface: A reggae fan humming along while saving cash, mentioned in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hums' suggests singing, but in British slang to hum is to smell bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinkard is an old word for a person who stinks, someone who smells offensively.

clue.text: Raised money when giving a speech

indicators.note: spoken aloud in a speech, the money word gives a word of the same sound

parts.note: bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: A politician collects funds during a fundraising address.
explanation.definitionFit: Children or animals that are bred have been brought up or reared.

clue.text: I see about newspaper Republican Party dreads?

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the exclamation is read backwards

parts.note: ah is an exclamation meaning I see
the i is a British newspaper
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone notices a Republican newspaper and the party's fears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreads' looks like a verb of fear; it is dreadlocks, and the question mark flags an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadlocks are a style of hair, and a hairdo is any style of arranging hair.

clue.text: Sacred texts, a set composed after Bible

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters behind the Bible abbreviation

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

indicators.note: composed means put together in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A collection of holy writings put together following the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avesta is the scripture of Zoroastrianism, a collection of religious writings.

clue.text: Special forces are surrounding lake for a dip

indicators.note: surrounding means going around, so the forces and area letters enclose the lake letter

parts.note: SAS is the Special Air Service, British special forces
L is the map abbreviation for lake
an are is a metric unit of area, A

explanation.surface: Commandos are encircling a lake to go for a swim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dip' suggests a swim, but salsa is a sauce for dipping.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a spicy tomato sauce served for dipping tortilla chips.

clue.text: A kind of dance? Go slowly if necessary

parts.note: tap is a style of dance
to inch is to move very slowly

explanation.surface: A dance instruction to take things slowly when needed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom at a pinch means if absolutely required, in an emergency.

clue.text: A couple of queens lay on a banquet perhaps

parts.note: a queen is a female cat
a couple of queens asks for a second one, ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Two queens hosting a royal feast.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to provide food and drink for a function, such as laying on a feast.

clue.text: It's from e.g. Tiber estuary, not Rhode Island

definitions.note: 'It' is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it; the 's is a link meaning is

parts.note: the Tiber is an Italian river, an example of something Italian

indicators.note: not removes the Rhode Island letters

parts.note: an estuary is a river mouth
RI is the US state abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: Something said to come from the mouth of the River Tiber rather than from an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like a pronoun but is the drinks name, as in gin and it, a British bar order.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the abbreviation for the sweet vermouth from Italy, used in the cocktail gin and it.

clue.text: River fish's name in part of Africa

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river
the 1988 comedy film is called A Fish Called Wanda

explanation.surface: Naming a river fish found in a region of Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Rwanda is a landlocked country in east-central Africa.

clue.text: Take drugs one's discovered in book

parts.note: to do drugs is to take them
gear is slang for drugs

explanation.surface: Someone takes drugs and is caught with them hidden in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog-ear is the turned-down corner of a page, which you find in a well-read volume.
